Treatment summary
The patient presented following a motor vehicle collision in which their vehicle was struck while turning left. They reported pain
and swelling of the wrist at the time of evaluation, and the mechanism of injury described is consistent with the force expected in
a crash of this type. Initial imaging and physical examination clearly confirmed a fracture of the wrist. The patient has no known
prior injury to this body region. Treatment was immobilization followed by a course of physical therapy, consistent with the usual
management for this fracture. Across eleven visits, care was tapered gradaully as strength and range of motion improved and pain
decreased. Billing records reflect single, appropriate charges for each service rendered, with no repeated billing for the same
services. At the most recent visit, the patient was improving and was discharged to a home exercise program with instructions to
return if symptoms worsened.

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.

- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
